Q: How to set central widget fill in the whole main window in Qt A:

The answers here seem not to understand the basics of Qt containers.

If you place a widget on the MainWindow in designer, then view the Object Inspector, click on MainWindow (the root component in this scenario), then right-click on that, the final item in the context menu is "Layout". Choose "Layout Horizontally" (for example).

The widget under the MainWindow (which by default will have been set as the central widget of the QMainWindow) will automatically expand to fill the whole of the QMainWindow, including when you resize the QMainWindow.

Actually it won't: by default there will be margins around it. These margins in fact below to the "layout" of the centralwidget: click on that in Object Inspector and then look at the section at the bottom of Property Editor, called "Layout". Change (for example) "layoutLeftMargin" from 9 (default at the time of writing) 100: you will see that the widget is now permanently positioned 100 pixels to the right of the left edge of the QMainWindow. Again, if you change the size of the QMainWindow, the size of the "central widget" widget will always retain that left margin.

Thus we see that a container determines the type of layout of its child components ... and yet the layout child components also control things like margins for their parent containers. Layouts are themselves "child components".

Q: Running an executable in Mac Terminal A:

The answer by Anubhav is great, but then I found I could not run the binary except from that directory. After searching I found that to do that you have to put the binary in a directory on the PATH. For those (like me) confused by that, here are Anubhav's instructions repeated with 2 additional steps for putting the binary in the PATH:

1). Move to the path of the file:

cd/PATH_OF_THE_FILE

2). Run the following command to set the file's executable bit using the chmod command:

chmod +x ./NAME_OF_THE_FILE

3). Run the following command to execute the file:

./NAME_OF_THE_FILE

The above only works if you run from that directory. To run from any directory

4). Find out what directories are on your PATH with

tr ':' '\n' <<< $PATH

5). Move your binary to one of those directories and then you can execute it without adding ./ -- ie, just use the name of the binary file; that is,

NAME_OF_THE_FILE

Q: NodeJS MSAL Authentication: 430 4.2.0 STOREDRV Mailbox Logon Failure When Sending Email via Exchange Online SMTP A:

Make sure the application has `ReadPermission` for the user, `FullAccess` isn't enough it seems

Add-MailboxPermission -Identity <identity> -User <application ID> -AccessRights FullAccess,ReadPermission
